details: The conflict between the United States and Iran has entered a dangerous new phase, with the US resuming "powerful" retaliatory strikes on Iran following Iranian attacks on American forces in Jordan. Saudi Arabia has reportedly joined military escalations against Tehran-backed proxies. This heightened tension is significantly impacting air travel, shipping, and energy markets, particularly raising concerns about crude oil supplies through the Strait of Hormuz. As a result, Brent and West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude oil prices climbed, driven by fears of supply disruptions. The geopolitical instability contributes to global market uncertainty and inflation risks.
title: US-Iran Conflict Escalates, Fueling Oil Price Volatility

details: The U.S. Federal Reserve maintained its benchmark interest rate at 3.50%-3.75% for the fifth consecutive meeting on July 29, 2026. However, the decision revealed a rare 9-3 split among the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) members, with three officials dissenting in favor of a 25-basis-point rate hike. This significant division signals ongoing concerns within the central bank about persistent inflation, partly due to higher energy costs stemming from the Middle East conflict. While the Fed Chairman emphasized data-driven decisions and limited forward guidance, the lack of clear direction is contributing to market uncertainty. Bitcoin remained largely range-bound around $64,000 following the announcement, showing some resilience despite stock market dips.
title: Federal Reserve Holds Rates, Internal Division Signals Inflation Concerns
